notes:
Phrase search is a FILTER, not a second scorer. quotedPhrases() reads the closed double-quoted
segments out of the raw query and tokenizes them with the shared analyzer; phraseDocs() walks
positions to find adjacency; phraseDocIds() intersects the phrases and hands back ids — or null,
meaning "no phrase, do not restrict". null vs the empty Set is load-bearing: conflating them makes
every unquoted query return nothing.

Algorithm: anchor on the RAREST term of the phrase (fewest postings), then for each of its documents
check that every other term has position start + its offset, where start = anchorPosition - anchorIndex.
Candidates can only shrink, so anchoring on the rare term is what keeps a phrase containing a
corpus-wide common word cheap. Other terms' postings are indexed into a doc -> positions Map once per
query, not scanned per document.

Judge-facing decision: an UNTERMINATED quote is not a phrase. Promoting it would turn one stray
character into a recall cliff (a phrase filter answers with a handful of documents; the same query
unquoted answers with ten), so a half-quoted query degrades to exactly the behaviour it had before
phrases existed. Same instinct for an empty quote ("" or " - "): dropped, not treated as an
unsatisfiable phrase that silently empties the answer.

Correctness rests on the index's position space, not on this module: title tokens and body tokens
are separated by one unused coordinate, so "last word of the title" + "first word of the body" is
never adjacent. Tested here against a hand-built reader (the semantics are the reader interface's,
not this index's) and against the real corpus with a brute-force scan as the oracle.
